hero.title: Appeals Information
hero.intro: Property owners have the right to appeal an assessment when they disagree with the value, uniformity, taxability, exemption denial, or other appealable items shown on an assessment notice.

notice.title: Important Deadline Information
text: Appeals must be filed within the deadline shown on the annual Notice of Assessment. Property owners should review their notice carefully and contact the Tax Assessor’s Office with questions before the deadline passes.
This page is intended as a general guide. Official filing requirements are controlled by Georgia law and the instructions on the assessment notice and appeal form.

process.title: How the Appeal Process Works
process.intro: The steps below provide a general overview of the property assessment appeal process.

steps.title: Review your Notice of Assessment
steps.text: Read the notice carefully and compare the property details, value, exemptions, and appeal deadline shown on the notice.

steps.title: Contact the Tax Assessor’s Office if you have questions
steps.text: Staff may be able to explain the assessment, review property record details, and help you understand what information may be useful.

steps.title: File a written appeal before the deadline
steps.text: Submit the appeal form or written appeal to the Tax Assessor’s Office by the deadline listed on the notice. Keep a copy for your records.

steps.title: Staff review
steps.text: The appraisal staff reviews the appeal, property record, supporting information, and any relevant market or property data.

steps.title: Board of Assessors review
steps.text: The Board of Assessors reviews the appeal and may make changes, offer a value, or forward the appeal according to the selected appeal path.

steps.title: Further appeal options
steps.text: If the appeal is not resolved at the local review stage, the appeal may proceed through the applicable appeal option selected by the property owner, such as the Board of Equalization or other available process.

infoCards.title: Before You File
infoCards.subtitle: Make sure the basic property information is correct.
items: Check the parcel number and property location.
Review land and building details shown on the property record.
Review exemptions and special assessment information, if applicable.
Note the appeal deadline printed on the assessment notice.

infoCards.title: How to Submit
infoCards.subtitle: Submit the completed appeal before the deadline.
text: Appeals should be submitted to the Hart County Tax Assessor’s Office. The appeal should identify the property, owner, reason for appeal, and preferred appeal option when required.
Contact the office for current submission options if you are unsure how to file.
